recognize_zh: 左側骨髓抹片可見成群的紅血球前驅細胞，其中有雙核、呈苜蓿葉狀的正染性紅母細胞（binucleated erythroblast）；右側臨床照片見手指痛風石變形與腳趾潰瘍。遺傳性貧血加上雙核紅母細胞，符合先天性造血不良性貧血第二型（CDA II），高紅血球更新率則導致續發性痛風。
features: Erythroid precursors at intermediate to late stages with round nuclei and polychromatophilic to orthochromatic cytoplasm
Binucleated erythroblast with two equal-sized round nuclei (lower right) and a small cluster of erythroid precursors (upper left)
Condensed, dark nuclear chromatin in the late erythroblasts; no megaloblastic open chromatin
Background red cells with marked anisopoikilocytosis, including ovalocytes, teardrop-like and fragmented forms
Composite clinical photographs: nodular tophaceous deformity of the fingers and an ulcerated, necrotic great toe
describe_en: Wright-Giemsa-stained marrow smear (left panel) shows erythroid precursors, including a binucleated late erythroblast with two equal round nuclei and a small cluster of maturing erythroblasts, set against red cells with marked anisopoikilocytosis. Nuclear chromatin is condensed without megaloblastic features, and no ringed sideroblast assessment is possible on this stain. The accompanying clinical photographs show tophaceous deformity of the fingers and an ulcerated toe. In a young transfused patient with consanguinity and normal hemoglobin electrophoresis, the findings are consistent with congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type II complicated by secondary tophaceous gout; confirmation requires SEC23B sequencing or SDS-PAGE band 3 analysis.

ddx.vs: CDA I shows internuclear chromatin bridges and spongy 'Swiss cheese' heterochromatin on electron microscopy rather than predominance of binucleated late erythroblasts.
Megaloblastic erythroblasts have open, finely stippled chromatin with nuclear-cytoplasmic asynchrony and are accompanied by giant metamyelocytes, which are absent here.
Thalassemia shows microcytic target cells and abnormal hemoglobin studies (raised HbA2/HbF), whereas this patient has normal electrophoresis and binucleated erythroblasts.
MDS occurs in older adults with multilineage dysplasia and clonal cytogenetic or molecular lesions, not a lifelong familial anemia.
